title: Borrowed Falls
mechanic: Catch a falling object's remaining fall distance in a jar. Pour it into a grounded object to make that object fall the same distance upward. Distance is conserved, so every ascent must be paid for with a descent.
loop: Route a crate through three shelves while keeping enough fall distance for the exit.
fun: Seeing a dangerous drop become useful fuel makes failures feel like discoveries.
prototype: One room, two crates, three jars and five platforms. Show stored distance as a ruler.
risk: Invisible units could make solutions feel arbitrary. Preview the exact landing before pouring.
story: You repair a mountain town whose elevators have forgotten which way is down.

title: Shadow Stitch
mechanic: Sew two objects together only where their moving shadows overlap. Rotating a lamp changes the joint's position without moving the objects. A stitched pair shares rotation until its shadows separate.
loop: Aim the lamp, stitch a bridge, then swing the joined pieces into a walkable route.
fun: The same scenery supports several surprising structures as the light angle changes.
prototype: Two lamps, four hinged planks and one exit. Draw joints directly on the shadows.
risk: Shadow contact needs a generous preview so perspective never hides a valid stitch.
story: A midnight tailor stitches a path across the roofs before sunrise unravels it.

title: Verb Garden
mechanic: Pull an object's active verb out as a physical seed. Plant SLIDE from an ice tile into a door or GROW from a vine into a staircase. Each seed removes that behavior from its donor.
loop: Harvest one behavior, choose its new host, and use the changed room to reach the gate.
fun: Trading useful behaviors creates readable chain reactions instead of collecting abstract keys.
prototype: A six-tile room and three verbs: slide, grow and bounce. Animate every transfer.
risk: Unclear host compatibility would encourage guessing. Mark all legal hosts when holding a seed.
story: An apprentice gardener cultivates actions rather than flowers in a derelict greenhouse.

title: Future Fold
mechanic: Fold the next five seconds of a moving platform's path like a paper strip. The platform then traverses that folded route in order. Its past trail is pinned and cannot be edited.
loop: Pause to fold a forecast, ride the result, then plan the next segment before it becomes past.
fun: A visible forecast turns timing puzzles into hands-on spatial editing.
prototype: One rail, three legal fold points and a passenger. Ghost the entire future path.
risk: Freeform folds are hard to predict. Begin with snapped right-angle folds and explicit clearance.
story: A paper railway carries stranded commuters through a map that is still being drawn.

title: Echo Debt
mechanic: Every action creates an echo that repeats it three turns later at the original location. You may postpone one echo, but that action's next echo arrives one turn sooner. Your queue is the puzzle board.
loop: Schedule pushes and door toggles so delayed echoes complete a route you cannot walk yourself.
fun: Yesterday's apparently useless move becomes the missing half of a coordinated plan.
prototype: A small grid, two switches and a visible three-slot action queue. Allow unlimited undo.
risk: Delayed actions can feel unfair. Show their affected cells and exact execution order.
story: A clock repairer works alongside the inconvenient echoes of their own hands.

title: Weight of Words
mechanic: Lift letters out of instruction signs and use their letter counts as physical weights. A sign loses the rule described by its missing word; moving STOP both disables a barrier and gives you a four-unit counterweight.
loop: Balance a lift while deciding which room rules you can afford to dismantle.
fun: Reading the level and reshaping it become one concrete physical action.
prototype: Three fixed signs, a seesaw and a lift. Use visible word tiles with printed weights.
risk: Avoid language trivia. Keep a small taught vocabulary and display weights rather than testing spelling.
story: A museum night porter rearranges the rules to rescue an exhibit trapped in storage.

title: Inside-Out Key
mechanic: Turn a container inside out to swap its contents with the matching shape of empty space around it. Objects retain their orientation. The useful resource is the precise negative space you arrange.
loop: Pack furniture around a box, invert it, and extract the newly captured passage.
fun: Empty gaps become tangible tools, inviting playful experiments with arrangement.
prototype: One box and three block shapes on a grid. Preview the positive and negative silhouettes.
risk: Spatial inversion is unfamiliar. Teach a single block before introducing nested containers.
story: A warehouse clerk ships missing rooms to buildings that need extra space.

title: Temperature Script
mechanic: A robot reads a route encoded as a metal rail's heat pattern: cold means left, warm straight, hot right. Heat diffuses while it travels, so you solve by timing both the writing and the reading.
loop: Heat segments, cool boundaries and launch the robot before the instructions blur.
fun: A route acts like a living program that can change mid-execution.
prototype: A ten-segment rail, three heat values and visible diffusion every turn.
risk: Continuous heat may obscure causality. Use discrete turns and a forecast of the next diffusion step.
story: A lighthouse keeper programs a delivery robot using the last warmth of the sun.

title: Perspective Pocket
mechanic: Pocket an object only while its silhouette fits a frame. Releasing it from a different frame changes its depth but preserves the silhouette's area, trading height for width and available clearance.
loop: Find a useful view, store a silhouette and unfold it into a bridge or support.
fun: A deliberate area constraint makes perspective tricks into repeatable construction tools.
prototype: Three fixed camera stations, one frame and four shapes. Show dimensions before release.
risk: Camera precision must not be the challenge. Snap viewpoints and reject unclear silhouettes.
story: A surveyor carries collapsed buildings as flat keepsakes and restores their missing paths.

title: Color Custody
mechanic: Each room rule is bound to a color token that must have exactly one owner. Swap the tokens of two objects to swap their rules, such as solid and permeable, without changing their shapes or positions.
loop: Pass rule ownership around obstacles until a solid route and a permeable exit coexist.
fun: Conserved rule tokens make spectacular transformations legible and strategically reversible.
prototype: Four labeled objects, three rule tokens and a swap preview. Include patterned color labels.
risk: Color alone excludes players. Pair every token with a unique symbol and text label.
story: A registrar untangles a city's misplaced building permits, one impossible doorway at a time.

title: Rumor Maze
mechanic: A door opens only when two messengers independently believe it is open. You route their sightlines to evidence, then block their view before contradictory evidence changes their belief. Knowledge has spatial inertia.
loop: Stage evidence, separate witnesses and reunite their claims at the destination door.
fun: Manipulating who knows what creates puzzles without requiring reflexes or hidden information.
prototype: Two messengers, three evidence windows and visible belief icons. No dialogue parser.
risk: Belief updates must be explicit. Animate the exact observation that changes a messenger's claim.
story: Two earnest couriers try to map a castle whose doors obey consensus.

title: Elastic Calendar
mechanic: Stretch one turn on a calendar to give a machine extra movement during that turn. The borrowed time compresses neighboring turns by the same amount. All machines share the calendar but have different movement rates.
loop: Redistribute a fixed time budget so several machines align on the same arrival turn.
fun: One edit can repair one machine's timing while creating an interesting problem for another.
prototype: A five-turn strip and three conveyors. Preview all arrivals after each time transfer.
risk: Arithmetic should stay visible. Use integer time blocks and limit edits to one-block transfers.
story: A stationmaster borrows minutes from quiet hours to save an impossible timetable.

title: Recoil Cartographer
mechanic: Your cannon fires pieces of the floor out of the arena. The recoil launches you in the opposite direction, while the fired tile becomes a temporary landing pad wherever it hits. Attack, movement and terrain creation are one shot.
loop: Carve a launch tile, aim a landing, and chain recoil hops through moving targets.
fun: Every spectacular jump leaves a useful piece of your route ahead of you.
prototype: One arena, six reusable floor tiles and stationary targets. Ghost both recoil and tile arcs.
risk: A missed shot could strand the player. Tiles return after a short timeout and a safe hub persists.
story: A demolition courier delivers parcels across a city by mailing the streets ahead.

title: Breath Bridge
mechanic: Exhaling extends a solid ribbon behind you; inhaling reels it back and pulls you toward its anchor. The same finite breath controls bridge length and grappling speed, so traversal alternates between laying and reclaiming a route.
loop: Lay a ribbon around obstacles, anchor it, then inhale to slingshot through the gap.
fun: A route becomes a spring you can improvise with rather than a fixed grappling point.
prototype: Three anchors, a visible breath meter and a single ribbon. Start without enemies.
risk: Breath should be a game meter, never require physical breath control or microphone input.
story: A kite spirit reconnects floating gardens using ribbons woven from wind.

title: Impact Orchard
mechanic: Parried attacks are planted as stationary buds. Each bud releases the captured attack along its original vector when another bud's blast touches it. You build a chain reaction by positioning parries.
loop: Catch several attacks, place their buds, then trigger a cascade through armored enemies.
fun: Defense becomes a creative way to compose a delayed offensive spectacle.
prototype: One enemy firing slow bolts, three bud slots and visible direction arrows.
risk: Chain reactions can become unreadable. Slow the first cascades and draw trigger links beforehand.
story: A guardian grows a defensive orchard from the weapons aimed at a sleeping village.

title: Speed Auction
mechanic: Trade slices of your current running speed for obstacles' future motion. Spending speed on a gate makes it slide open at that same speed; reclaiming the slice freezes it and restores your momentum.
loop: Split momentum among gates while retaining enough speed to clear the resulting course.
fun: A racing line doubles as a sequence of dynamic investments in the track itself.
prototype: One runner, two sliding gates and a visible speed allocation bar. Include instant retry.
risk: Momentum debt needs clear feedback. Keep the total speed visible across runner and gates.
story: A street racer negotiates passage with a road that accepts velocity as currency.

title: Hitbox Herder
mechanic: Your vulnerable hitbox is a small creature that follows your painted avatar on a tether. Damage checks the creature, not the avatar. Swing it around cover while using your avatar to distract attacks.
loop: Bait a volley, shelter your hitbox and swing the tether through the next safe pocket.
fun: Being visually bold while protecting a separate fragile companion creates playful near misses.
prototype: A circular arena, one tether, slow bullets and clearly separate avatar and hitbox art.
risk: Never imply the avatar is invulnerable by accident. Teach both entities with labeled hazards.
story: A stage magician protects their wandering shadow during a dangerously enthusiastic performance.

title: Silence Skater
mechanic: Noise you make becomes physical ridges in the ground after one second. Sliding quietly preserves a smooth track; stomping deliberately creates ramps that redirect you and the chasing enemies.
loop: Read the chase, stamp a ramp and arrive when your own sound becomes solid terrain.
fun: Your mistakes and flourishes sculpt a course you can exploit moments later.
prototype: A looping track, one pursuer and two noise levels. Show every pending ridge as a ghost.
risk: Audio must not be required. Visualize noise amplitude, delay and resulting ramp height.
story: A roller courier races through a city where every echo eventually settles into stone.

title: Damage Tailor
mechanic: Cut damage zones out of a visible attack pattern and sew those patches into your shield. Removing a patch makes the remaining attack faster; wearing it blocks only the same shape and orientation.
loop: Choose a cut, rotate the patch and intercept the accelerated remainder of the attack.
fun: A defense is handcrafted from the exact threat you are facing.
prototype: Three slow geometric attack patterns, one cut per attack and a rotatable shield patch.
risk: Complex shapes could overwhelm reaction time. Begin with rectangles and offer a planning pause.
story: An arena costume maker survives a tournament by tailoring armor from hostile choreography.

title: Checkpoint Catapult
mechanic: Place your next respawn point as a physical projectile. It must land safely before you can return there, and its trajectory gains the distance you traveled since the previous checkpoint. Progress literally throws your future farther.
loop: Run a risky segment, launch the checkpoint and choose whether to follow or reset to it.
fun: Respawning becomes an expressive movement tool with a visible, earned range.
prototype: A short obstacle course and one checkpoint ball. Preview safe landing zones.
risk: Bad checkpoints must not trap a run. Keep the previous safe point until the new landing validates.
story: An explorer sends a little beacon ahead into places their feet have not yet reached.

title: Rotation Relay
mechanic: Steal an enemy's angular velocity on contact and spend it rotating your entire local arena. The enemy stops turning while you hold it; rotating the arena redirects gravity for everything inside a marked radius.
loop: Catch a spin, roll hazards away and rotate yourself onto the next surface.
fun: An enemy's characteristic motion becomes a satisfying terrain control resource.
prototype: A square room, one spinning turret and a bounded rotation field. Use ninety-degree milestones.
risk: Camera rotation may be uncomfortable. Keep the camera fixed and rotate the world within it.
story: A mechanic winds broken planets back into alignment using borrowed spins.

title: Combo Compass
mechanic: Successful hits rotate your movement compass one quarter turn, but missed hits rotate the enemy's compass instead. Directions remain visible on a compass rose, making a combo a route-planning instrument.
loop: Plan a hit sequence whose compass changes carry you through the arena's safe lanes.
fun: Combat rhythm produces surprising but learnable movement puzzles.
prototype: Four lanes, stationary training targets and a large compass. Offer a slow practice mode.
risk: Remapped controls can frustrate players. Preview the next mapping and keep rotations discrete.
story: A dancer duels in a ballroom whose floor directions follow the beat of landed strikes.

title: Friction Painter
mechanic: Scrape friction off a surface while sliding and paint it onto another surface. A slippery floor can become a grippy wall, but the total friction in the room never changes.
loop: Harvest a fast slide, paint a climbing strip and switch between speed and traction routes.
fun: Movement leaves tangible materials for the next movement trick.
prototype: One floor, two walls and a three-unit brush. Display traction with both color and texture.
risk: Traction must agree with collision. Keep three discrete levels with clearly different movement.
story: A climbing artist restores grip to an icebound city one painted foothold at a time.

title: Delay Duelist
mechanic: Aim attacks by placing their impact spots in a queue rather than firing immediately. Dodging through a queued spot advances it one slot, so your evasive route also edits the order of your offense.
loop: Queue three impacts, weave through selected spots and release a reordered combination.
fun: The best escape route can become the most stylish attack sequence.
prototype: One dueling opponent, three impact markers and a visible queue. Permit canceled placements.
risk: Queue edits need instant feedback. Number markers and animate their order changing on a dodge.
story: A fencer fights with appointments for blows that have yet to happen.

title: Promise Market
mechanic: Build machines using promises of future resources instead of current stock. Every promise is also a physical delivery route that enemies can obstruct. Broken promises dismantle only the machine they financed.
loop: Lay a route, pledge its future yield and defend the commitments that matter most.
fun: Expansion is an exciting spatial bet with visible consequences rather than hidden debt.
prototype: A small map, two resources and three machines. Draw every promise's delivery route.
risk: Failures could cascade too harshly. Separate obligations and show deadlines several turns ahead.
story: A frontier settlement is built on deliveries its founders have not harvested yet.

title: Attention Town
mechanic: Only buildings inside your movable spotlight actively produce. Unattended buildings store potential work as pressure; bringing them back into focus releases that backlog as a burst that nearby buildings must absorb.
loop: Sweep attention between districts and prepare storage before releasing a pressured building.
fun: A city's tempo follows your attention, making dramatic bursts a planning reward.
prototype: Six buildings, a two-building spotlight and visible pressure gauges. Use turn-based sweeps.
risk: Avoid punishing reading time. Pressure advances by turns, not by where the real mouse points.
story: A sleepy mayor keeps a clockwork town awake with one wandering beam of daylight.

title: Border Barter
mechanic: Negotiate territory by trading individual border segments rather than land tiles. A district's resources depend on what its border encloses, while the number of available border pieces is fixed.
loop: Borrow a neighbor's boundary, reshape an enclosure and negotiate back before supplies run low.
fun: One clever boundary move can reorganize several districts without a battle.
prototype: A twelve-tile map, three districts and a fixed stock of edge pieces.
risk: Enclosure math must be legible. Highlight resource changes before committing a boundary edit.
story: Three tiny kingdoms share an estate and a comically insufficient supply of fences.

title: Memory Fleet
mechanic: Ships navigate only routes they remember. Move a route memory from one ship to another to give it access, but the donor then forgets that route. Memories have limited slots and must travel physically with couriers.
loop: Deliver route memories ahead of cargo, then reclaim them for the next convoy.
fun: Logistics revolves around transporting knowledge as carefully as goods.
prototype: Four ports, three ships and two memory slots per ship. Display known routes on each hull.
risk: Forgetting must not strand a ship silently. Warn before transfers and preserve its current return leg.
story: A fleet of forgetful vessels reconnects an archipelago by exchanging little bottles of directions.

title: Symbiosis Siege
mechanic: Enemy units consume your waste and excrete the materials you need. You arrange habitats to steer them instead of destroying them; overfeeding makes them split and underfeeding makes them attack your production.
loop: Balance waste routes, guide a useful herd and harvest its outputs before the next siege wave.
fun: A dangerous invader can become the missing link in a satisfying production chain.
prototype: One enemy species, two waste sources and three habitat tiles. Expose feeding thresholds.
risk: The economy needs recoverable mistakes. Let players lure excess creatures into a safe holding area.
story: A besieged botanist discovers that the invaders make surprisingly excellent compost.

title: Vote Velocity
mechanic: Citizens vote by physically walking toward a proposal. Their votes count only while they are moving, so streets, congestion and rest stops determine the duration and strength of a policy rather than a static popularity number.
loop: Lay public routes, pace the procession and keep two compatible policies moving together.
fun: Urban layout becomes a visible, lively instrument for shaping temporary consensus.
prototype: Ten citizens, two proposals and a tiny road grid. Offer a turn-by-turn movement forecast.
risk: Do not hide decisions in crowd AI. Show each citizen's destination and exactly when a vote counts.
story: A town council replaces speeches with cheerful civic parades through its winding streets.

title: Entropy Post
mechanic: Move disorder between factories as sealed parcels. A clean factory works precisely but creates disorder; a messy one converts disorder into bulk output. Parcels leak slowly in transit, so routing determines production quality.
loop: Schedule precise and messy jobs, deliver their byproducts and balance the shared disorder budget.
fun: An unwanted byproduct becomes a useful input through a well-timed delivery network.
prototype: Two factory types, three courier routes and visible parcel leakage each turn.
risk: Abstract disorder needs concrete effects. Limit it to three labeled levels with predictable output.
story: A postal service keeps a miniature universe tidy by delivering its mess to places that enjoy it.

title: Queue Kingdom
mechanic: Units share one initiative queue. Moving a unit costs its queue position, and lending that position lets another unit act immediately. A formation's physical adjacency determines who may receive the loan.
loop: Arrange a relay formation, lend turns through it and break the enemy's turn supply chain.
fun: Support units create clever tactical combinations by passing opportunities rather than damage buffs.
prototype: Three units per side on a small grid. Keep the initiative queue always visible.
risk: Infinite relay loops would erase tactics. Each unit can receive only one lent turn per round.
story: A chess club's pieces learn to be punctual for one another instead of taking turns alone.

title: Forecast Farm
mechanic: Plant crops in weather forecasts rather than soil. Moving a forecast card changes which field receives its weather; harvested crops erase the forecast they consumed, altering every later field's irrigation plan.
loop: Assign weather, commit crops and harvest in an order that preserves the next useful forecast.
fun: A harvest is both a payoff and an interesting edit to the future.
prototype: Three fields and five forecast cards. Show the changed weather sequence before harvesting.
risk: Prevent long-range surprises. Keep the full short forecast visible and allow undo before advancing.
story: A cloud farmer grows a village's meals inside the promises made by tomorrow's sky.

title: Repair Rebellion
mechanic: Every repair transfers a machine's broken behavior into a reusable glitch tile. Install that tile elsewhere to intentionally inherit the fault, such as a conveyor that reverses every third turn. No fault disappears from the system.
loop: Fix a critical machine, place its glitch where it helps and plan production around conserved faults.
fun: Imperfections become expressive tools instead of chores to eliminate.
prototype: Three machines and three deterministic faults. Preview an entire six-turn production cycle.
risk: Fault stacking can become opaque. Allow one glitch per machine and give each a distinct icon.
story: A maintenance crew rescues an old factory by finding better homes for its bad habits.

title: Distance Dividend
mechanic: Trade routes earn resources only for distance removed from the network. Straightening one route spends its former detour as construction credit, but every new building lengthens nearby routes and creates fresh opportunities to optimize.
loop: Build a useful detour, shorten it efficiently and reinvest the saved distance into a new district.
fun: Growth and optimization feed each other through a resource you can see on the map.
prototype: Four nodes, editable road bends and one construction type. Display saved distance on each edit.
risk: Repeated edits must not mint credit. Track the historical shortest credited distance per route.
story: A cartographer funds a growing town with the miles they save its weary travelers.

title: Season Custodian
mechanic: Seasons occupy tiles as movable pieces. Passing summer through a tile ripens it, while moving summer away freezes its growth at that stage. You have one piece per season and their paths cannot cross.
loop: Route the four seasons through fields in a useful order without blocking their next journey.
fun: A farm becomes a choreography of mobile environments rather than a passive timer.
prototype: A four-by-four grid, four season pieces and two crop types. Show each crop's required sequence.
risk: Deadlocks need recovery. Permit a neutral holding tile and a reversible planning phase.
story: Four small weather spirits take turns tending a world too small for a normal calendar.
